Subject: Dedicated sizing simulation for NorthStar: surge-margin & tail-latency checks

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for taking the time last week. To get a precise Dedicated (reserved GPU) recommendation we need a short traffic snapshot from you so we can model tokens/sec distributions and tail latency impact. Can you confirm the items below for your production workload?

Quick ask (one-line answers are fine):
- Typical requests/day and % during peak hour
- Average/median tokens per request and 95th tokens per request
- Typical KV-cache hit % for conversational reuse or repeated prompts
- Any scheduled daily/weekly batch-bursts (dates/times) and expected concurrency
- Which model variant you want pinned on Dedicated (open-lm-13b / oss-13B-quant / other)

Our initial sizing approach will:
- Estimate sustained tokens/sec and a 1-hour peak tokens/sec window
- Run a tail-latency SLO fit (p95/p99) assuming FP16 and 8-bit quant variants
- Recommend a slab count and recommended headroom (%) for canary and burst windows

I attached a short request form to make this easier. If you prefer, paste values into a reply and I will run a first-pass simulation today.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Sergio —

Thanks, see answers inline from our telemetry:
- Typical requests/day: ~1.8M requests/day, with ~9% of traffic in peak hour
- Tokens per request: median 42 tokens, mean 68 tokens, 95th = 240 tokens
- KV-cache hit: around 40% overall (conversational reuse), for certain customers >60%
- Scheduled bursts: product release events cause 10–15 minute spikes ~3x baseline at irregular times (next planned: 2025-09-02, unknown hour)
- Model: prefer to pin a quantized 13B (oss-13B-8bit) but can run FP16 variant if needed for p95 compliance

One note: we have two traffic classes — premium (10% of requests) needs 200ms p95; standard is 400ms p95. Premium traffic is tagged in the request header (x-ns-priority: high).

Attached a CSV export with an hour-by-hour token histogram for the last 30 days. Let us know if you want raw logs.

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@northstar.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Aug 2025 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing simulation for NorthStar: surge-margin & tail-latency checks

Jordan —

Appreciate the data, that’s exactly what we need. I ran a first-pass tokens/sec and tail-latency simulation against two variants: oss-13B-8bit (our latency profile with quantized kernels) and fp16-13B. Summary below, full simulation attached.

High-level summary (assumptions):
- Baseline sustained tokens/sec (24h avg): 1.8M requests/day * 68 tokens/request / 86400s ≈ 1,417 tokens/sec sustained
- Peak-hour sustained tokens/sec (9% of daily within hour): 0.09 * 1.8M * 68 / 3600s ≈ 3,060 tokens/sec sustained in peak hour
- Short burst peak (3x baseline for 10–15m): transient tokens/sec ~9,180 tokens/sec
- KV-cache reuse reduces model decode tokens by ~40% on average; effective decode tokens/sec reduced proportionally in cached flows

Latency / SLO fit (p95 target):
- oss-13B-8bit: modeled p95 = 210ms at 3,060 tokens/sec with 20% slab utilization; p99 = 510ms under same conditions
- fp16-13B: modeled p95 = 145ms at 3,060 tokens/sec; p99 = 360ms

Slab / GPU sizing:
- For oss-13B-8bit (recommended by cost): 6 slabs (each slab = 4xA100-like GPUs) to meet premium p95=200ms with ~25% headroom for bursts; this yields comfortable autoscaling margin for 3x short bursts with KV caching
- For fp16-13B (recommended if premium p95 must be conservative): 4 slabs to meet premium p95, lower P99 tail and simpler QoS routing (but ~30% higher monthly cost)

Recommended next steps:
1) If NorthStar wants to minimize cost and accept quantized p99 degradation, start with oss-13B-8bit, provision 6 slabs, and run a 2-week canary routing 20% of premium traffic to Dedicated.
2) If premium SLAs are hard requirement, provision 4 slabs fp16 + 2 spare slabs for burst buffer (can be idle, keep warm) — total 6 slabs but with different performance characteristics.
3) Instrument priority routing header and KV-cache metrics so we can increase effective headroom for premium traffic without doubling slabs.

I attached the simulation CSV (ns_surge_simulation_v1.csv) — contains per-slab TPS mapping and expected p95/p99 under different KV-hit and concurrency assumptions. Please review; Marissa & Ben are on Cc to validate GPU sku and SLA framing.

Best,
Sergio
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: ns_surge_simulation_v1.csv (columns: timestamp, tokens_sec_baseline, kv_hit_pct, model_variant, slab_count, slab_util_pct, modeled_p95_ms, modeled_p99_ms)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Sergio / Jordan —

Quick validation from infra/cost:
- I ran the CSV through our slab-cost engine with updated GPU SKUs (A100 equivalent, spot vs reserved pricing). Cost difference between oss-13B-8bit on 6 slabs vs fp16 on 6 slabs with 2 warm spares is ~28% monthly.
- One adjustment: telemetry suggests NorthStar's KV-cache hit for premium customers reads closer to 55% (not 40%) when we filter by authenticated sessions. With 55% hit, oss-13B-8bit meets premium p95 comfortably at 5 slabs (not 6) for the typical peak-hour profile. That reduces cost materially.

Operational asks before we finalize:
- Can you confirm what percentage of premium traffic is actually routed with session cookies (we used 75% session-tagged in the model)?
- Agree to the 2-week 20% canary for dedicated traffic routing? If yes, we can generate a DocuSign amendment and a dedicated SLA addendum.

Jordan — I dropped a DocuSign draft link in related_links for the initial reserved slab term (6 months). If you want a 12-month commit we can optimize pricing further.

If you confirm session-routing and canary, we will update the simulation and provide a final purchase SKU list by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
